method: The real chat page (app.py through the I-5 launcher, switches set in the launcher process only, no .env) was driven in the built-in browser with Developer mode on; for every turn the visible answer, the citation chips and the Developer panel rows were read from the page DOM. No model client is configured, so every legacy answer is the no-key reply; what is checked is the served path, the Plan F outcome, the document and page chips, the domain and the diagnostics. Latencies here are not measurements (the test suite ran at the same time).

observations: Guide page chips carry the page's heading as the section label (for example 'Page 1 · BLACKBOARD ULTRA FACULTY SHORT GUIDE'); it is the heading printed on that page, not a handbook section. On a guide's first page the heading repeats the document title, which reads redundantly under the document chip (cosmetic; not changed in PF-2).
The Developer 'Source ids' row lists the source of every evidence item, while the chips show only the cited pages; the two can differ when a lower-ranked item comes from another document.
No Plan F answer rested on guide evidence in any mode, as the frozen specialists' source guard predicts; every guide question fell back to the legacy path.
